title: Microsoft Entra: Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO count as a standalone second factor for MFA
notes: claim 43: severity major on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing background and authentication strength control are supported. It should acknowledge conflicting Learn guidance about second-factor support and replace its unsupported promise of fewer step-up prompts with the documented removal of the additional-credential requirement.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The change reaches users who already hold these methods without an administrator switching on the new recognition behaviour.
claims.quote: Users who have only WHfB or macOS PSSO are now treated as MFA-capable and will no longer be automatically prompted to register another method.

claims.claim: The change lets more users rely on phishing-resistant sign-in without registering an extra method.
claims.quote: so more of your users can rely on strong, phishing-resistant sign-in without registering an extra method.

claims.claim: A device-bound credential cannot provide a second option on another device or operating system.
claims.quote: These credentials stay on the device where they're created. They aren't synced to other devices and can't be used from another device through cross-device QR code sign-in.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes authentication changes, not new application data access.
claims.quote: Windows Hello for Business (WHfB) and macOS Platform SSO (macOS PSSO) can now satisfy multifactor authentication as a standalone second factor.

claims.claim: Require authentication strength determines acceptable method combinations for access to a resource.
claims.quote: Administrators can specify an authentication strength to access a resource by creating a Conditional Access policy with the Require authentication strength control.

claims.claim: WHfB or platform credential is included in all three built-in authentication strengths.
claims.quote:
| Authentication method combination | MFA strength | Passwordless MFA strength | Phishing-resistant MFA strength |

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn says a user who initially signs in with a password is not prompted for required WHfB and must restart and select Sign-in options.
claims.quote: the user isn't prompted to sign in with Windows Hello for Business. The user needs to restart the session, select Sign-in options, and select a method that the authentication strength requires.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes no autonomous actions.
claims.quote: With this change, WHfB and macOS PSSO work on their own for those scenarios

claims.claim: System-preferred authentication ranks registered credentials.
claims.quote: The system evaluates which credentials are registered for the user and selects the highest-ranked method for each authentication step.

claims.claim: System-preferred authentication does not offer WHfB on non-Windows devices or macOS PSSO on non-macOS devices.
claims.quote: Windows Hello for Business and Microsoft Entra passkey on Windows aren't offered on non-Windows devices, including a Mac, iPhone, iPad, Android device, or Linux device. macOS Platform SSO isn't offered on non-macOS devices.

claims.claim: The roadmap record names no separate licence, meter or price for this change.
claims.quote: With this change, WHfB and macOS PSSO work on their own for those scenarios, so more of your users can rely on strong, phishing-resistant sign-in without registering an extra method.
